principles: Bundled is the default until independent adoption or release evidence exists.
A composition of capabilities is a playbook, not an atomic skill repository.
An executable stateful system becomes its own Work or joins an existing system Work; the Hub retains a thin skill adapter.
A recipe for one private environment is not a reusable public capability until generalized.
Repository promotion never changes the skill identity recorded by the Hub.

assessments.target: Skills Hub instruction adapter over the Library-owned CLI
assessments.reason: The Library owns registry behavior and validation. The Hub owns discovery and installation of the bounded registration instructions, with an exact reviewed source pointer.
One bounded static publication capability with an explicit public boundary and exact artifact readback; the Library is the first consumer.

This is a multi-step CMUX operating scenario with machine workspace examples; Herdr is the current workspace substrate.
The capability is one phase of a larger delivery sequence and communicates through stories.json rather than an independent tool contract.
The file is a private launcher/model inventory, not a stable executable capability, and its agent paths are environment-specific.

evidence.summary: All 28 registered skill definitions were read directly before classification.
The three task/state entries were compared at documentation, executable, configuration, schema, and test boundaries.
No folder currently proves independent adoption, ownership, release cadence, and a coherent standalone verification surface strongly enough for immediate repository promotion.
